title: Strings and show arrangements in the 1931 band
summary: Cecil Irwin wrote string arrangements; a classical soprano performed.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, let's go back a little bit, talk about that 1931 band, which was such a great band. You had mentioned last week that Larry Dixon doubled cello.

And that you would have like two clarinets, cello, guitar, bass, you know, string bass in the rhythm section, and you'd get this different sound. What did you use that group for? You know, say at the Grand Terrace, was it just a change of pace?

Like Cecil did all the arranging when it come to strings. And that's just the way Cecil would make his arrangement. He would -- maybe the first introduction, first chorus would be strings, you know. Woodwind. Then we'd go into the swing part, with them changing the saxophone.
Yeah, that was quite unique for that time.
And also, come in handy on the show. Like we have your sopranos and your different artists. Those arrangements was just like, say, downtown. With the strings, you know.
Well, would you have some acts that would do sort of like semi-classical things?
Yes. Oh, yeah, we had -- what the heck was that name? Marie Brown, she did classicals. She was a classical soprano.
